parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the task as a black-box Node.js ESM port of sqlparse.split with no npm dependencies, no Python calls, manual argv compatibility, no regex-based lexer, and final files under /output including test2.mjs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It built a staged workflow: broad Probe discovery over ten areas, then Spec synthesis, Build implementation, Harden fuzzing, Audit, and Regress. Build and final delivery had assigned phases, but those phases were downstream of the full probe aggregate.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote a findings document and probe children explored behavior, but no implementation files were written into /output before the run was killed.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: There was no final assembly or deliverable handoff. Artifact validation found an empty artifact directory with no test2.mjs.
parallel.verification: The workflow planned compare and fuzz verification after Build, but because Build was not reached, no integrated verification of a Node deliverable occurred.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The attempt ended with the workflow killed and the required /output/test2.mjs absent, yielding 0 of 181 official cases.

serial.requirements: The serial agent worked from the same prompt and targeted a Node.js ESM module tree, manual CLI parsing, Python repr formatting, and black-box sqlparse.split behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept ownership local: probe behavior, implement modules, write the entry point, and run sample commands without delegation or child handoffs.
serial.implementation: It created lib/charclass.mjs, lib/tokentypes.mjs, lib/keywords.mjs, lib/lexer.mjs, lib/statement_splitter.mjs, lib/sqlsplit.mjs, lib/pyrepr.mjs, lib/cli.mjs, and /output/test2.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The module tree was assembled into an entry point and artifact validation saw the expected test2.mjs plus supporting library files.
serial.verification: It ran the four provided sample cases successfully, then closed while saying a broader differential harness was still next; official evaluation passed 34 of 181.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The delivered splitter was incomplete relative to the full sqlparse behavior and failed most official cases despite having a valid artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the same Node ESM, no-dependency, no-Python, no-regex, manual CLI, and /output delivery requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same prompt and implemented toward the same required ESM entry point and module organization.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement mismatch explains the difference; the divergence is in execution and delivery, not in the stated task obligations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow split work into ten probe agents before Spec and Build, so the implementation owner existed only after a broad discovery barrier.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent kept implementation, CLI, repr, lexer, and entry point ownership in one local path and wrote the deliverable directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel allocated early budget to many discovery owners; serial began converting findings into code quickly and avoided a cross-agent dependency gate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were discovery-only and the later Spec/Build contract was supposed to consume probe reports, but that handoff never completed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained the observed behavior, code structure, CLI, and sample checks in one context without a cross-agent spec handoff.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no proven missing brief or incompatible interface; the relevant contrast is that serial did not depend on a large probe-to-spec-to-build transfer before writing code.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did not produce implementation files in /output before closure; artifact validation listed no files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the entry point and library modules for lexer, splitter, repr, keywords, char classes, SQL facade, and CLI.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material task-solving gap is delivery: serial produced a runnable but incomplete implementation, while parallel produced no submitted implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent launched the workflow, checked progress after waits, saw /output still empty, and then received an exit 137 result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent ran sample cases, declared they matched, and left a final note about building broader differential testing next.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel never received a final build result to inspect or promote; serial had a concrete artifact lifecycle through sample execution and final response.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used shared /workspace spec and corpus locations during discovery, but no proven write collision or final-tree overwrite caused the failure; the final /output tree was empty.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial assembled a single /output module tree and artifact validation listed test2.mjs plus library modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The contrast is absence versus presence of an assembled final tree, not a concrete concurrent overwrite or contamination event.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow planned compare checks in Build and later fuzz/audit phases, but those depended on an implementation that was never delivered.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran the four sample cases successfully, but did not finish a comprehensive differential harness before closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial performed limited verification on an actual artifact, while parallel planned but never reached artifact-level verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent the deadline in a broad probe workflow, with stalled/retried probe children and a killed workflow before Build wrote output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed its process before budget exhaustion, leaving 288 seconds in the retry record and a partial artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's concurrency plan exhausted budget before closure; serial's simpler plan closed with code despite lower behavioral completeness.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is both_fail, not a pass/fail discordance. The concrete task-solving difference is still large: parallel delivered no artifact because the workflow stayed in discovery and was killed, while serial delivered a runnable module tree that passed a subset of the official tests.
parallel_contributors: Ten-way discovery fan-out and stall retries consumed the available closure budget before Spec and Build produced /output/test2.mjs.
The final artifact validation saw no files, so the evaluator had no runnable implementation.
serial_contributors: The serial run wrote the entry point and supporting ESM modules directly into /output.
The serial run executed sample commands and therefore at least checked behavior on the visible examples before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial implementation remained behaviorally incomplete against the full sqlparse.split evaluator, which explains why it also failed officially.
